title: autoscaler-queue-backpressure-led-to-burst-credit-depletion-and-customer-503s
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Customer-facing 503s for three large Dedicated tenants between 2025-01-31 21:10 UTC and 2025-02-01 02:45 UTC. Root cause traces to two interacting regressions in the Dedicated autoscaling and burst allocation path: (1) the autoscaler observed only active allocations and ignored in-flight queued requests after a middleware reorder, causing under-scaling when admission queues started to grow; (2) burst_credit_accounting only refilled credits on slot allocation events and never on request completion when the request passed through the admission queue, causing burst credits to drain and fail future grants. Together these led to sustained headroom shortfall and blocked burst grants in reserved pools, which then cascaded to request rejections and customer escalations.
root_cause: Autoscaler uses active_slot_count metric emitted by allocation service; recent change moved the admission queue (request buffer) ahead of the allocation sampler for latency reasons. The sampler therefore saw fewer active slots and did not trigger scale-up. Separately, burst credit refill logic assumed credits were returned on allocation completion events; queued requests that waited in the admission buffer never triggered completion events until they were assigned a slot, so credits were effectively withheld and slowly depleted under sustained queueing.
fix: Hotfix v2025.02.01-01: (a) Autoscaler change to consume 'observed_demand' which adds queued_request_count to active_slot_count. (b) Burst accounting patch to credit refunds on request admission completion and on explicit timeout/abort paths. (c) Added conservative safety headroom: temporary +15% emergency tokens for all reserved pools for 72 hours to avoid repeated customer impact while we validate. Deploy sequence: canary to dedicated-staging -> region canaries -> global prod. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 , https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/657
rollout: Canary deployed to us-west-2 dedicated pool cluster at 2025-02-02 03:20 UTC. Metrics validated for 4h (queue length stable, burst grants resumed). Gradual rollout to other regions completed by 2025-02-02 09:00 UTC. Emergency headroom policy toggled on 2025-02-02 03:25 UTC and will be auto-removed on 2025-02-05 unless rolled into config.
comments: 2025-02-01 02:55 UTC — Ava Chen: Initial triage: multiple tenants in reserved pools reported elevated 5xx starting ~21:10 UTC. Pager rotation confirmed allocator errors 'burst_grant_denied' and autoscaler logs show no recent scale-ups despite queue growth. Opening ENG-881234 to track.

2025-02-01 03:10 UTC — Ravi Singh: Replicated symptom in staging by replaying tenant traffic with delayed response backend. Observed queue length upstream of allocator increasing while allocator active_slots remained flat. Initiated targeted logging and increased metrics retention for admission and allocation samplers.

2025-02-01 04:05 UTC — Diego Morales: Identified middleware reorder deploy (internal rollout earlier that day) that moved admission buffer before the sampler. Created hypothesis: sampler undercounts demand. Confirmed via sampling traces.

2025-02-01 04:40 UTC — Sofia Patel (SRE): Observed burst_credit metrics: credits_total decaying without expected refills. Traced to refund path not firing for queued requests — refunds only occurred on slot release event which never happened for queued requests until they were assigned. Filed allocator PR to add refund on admission completion.

2025-02-01 05:15 UTC — Ravi Singh: Implemented patch to autoscaler to sum queued_request_count and active_slots as observed_demand. Also wired in a safety headroom toggle. Deployed patch to canary cluster for validation.

2025-02-02 07:50 UTC — Customer Success (Lena O'Connor): Sent initial incident notification to impacted customers with mitigation steps and timeline. Two customers acknowledged and requested postmortem when available.
2025-02-04 12:30 UTC — Security Review (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed no customer data was exposed during incident. No security escalation required.

2025-02-06 09:00 UTC — Ava Chen: Running additional load tests to validate edge cases: long-lived queued requests with frequent cancellations, sudden large bursts with zero warm pool. Tests passing on staging with patched accounting and autoscaler.
2025-02-08 11:20 UTC — Ravi Singh: Drafted follow-up plan and scheduled retro. Requesting assignment of related implementation work for better chaos testing and alerting improvements (see followups).
followups: Add end-to-end simulation harness that models admission queue + allocation sampler interactions (owner: ENG-runtime, estimate: 5)
Create integration test that injects queued_request_count into autoscaler sampling loop (owner: ENG-autoscaler, estimate: 3)
Audit other metrics that only count active allocations to find similar blindspots (owner: ENG-infra, estimate: 4)
Remove emergency headroom toggle after validation and replace with policy-driven burst reallocation (owner: ENG-allocator, due_date: 2025-02-28)
Postmortem and customer-facing root-cause writeup due 2025-02-12 (owner: Ava Chen)
Add alert: high queued_request_count to active_slots ratio with playbook to toggle headroom and force scale-up (owner: SRE)
Performance regression test to ensure admission reorder doesn't re-introduce sampler blindspot in future deploys (owner: ENG-ci)
